title: Tarot of Intervals
source: pentacles.pdf, pentacles-reading-key.pdf and pentacles-print-A4.pdf as delivered. cards/: composed fronts rendered from the PDF pages at 300 dpi; art/: embedded illustrations extracted unmodified (1024 x 1536). The illustrator's own pentacles.json (prompts, hashes) was not in the delivery.
reading: Pentacles give material conditions a visible form: what can take root, circulate, be worked, kept, enjoyed and handed on. A reserve can help; an opening can matter. Care, skill and possession have different demands. Red marks an intervention without certifying its outcome.
note: Titles, keywords, symbolism, Opening/Snag, questions and Goetic associations as the illustrator's key gives them. These cards were not drafted by Claude first; the key says they introduce no additional cipher.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.title: The Rooted Possibility
cards.symbolism: A single pentacle rests in a living root cradle. Its red seed has somewhere to begin, but the supports must remain able to bear it. Possibility is already material: it has weight, conditions and a place to grow.
cards.upright: A workable beginning; a resource that can take root; support made available.
cards.reversed: Treating potential as a finished return; offering a seed without conditions for growth.
cards.question: What would let this possibility become something you can sustain?

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.title: The Living Balance
cards.symbolism: Two pentacles hang at different heights while a keeper adjusts their pivot. Balance appears as an ongoing relation rather than a final level position. Some demands move together; others must take turns.
cards.upright: Flexible priorities; resources moved with changing demands; an adjustable arrangement.
cards.reversed: Constant adjustment without relief; keeping everything moving at the expense of what matters.
cards.question: What needs adjusting, and what could be allowed to wait?

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.title: The Agreed Work
cards.symbolism: Three makers fit three discs into one frame. Shared work requires more than being present together: its joints must make sense to more than one pair of hands. The visible red seam leaves room for further repair.
cards.upright: Complementary abilities; a joint task understood; skill made usable by others.
cards.reversed: Unspoken standards; expertise that cannot be shared; agreement assumed before the work is tested.
cards.question: What must be understood together for this joint to hold?

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
cards.title: The Breathing Store
cards.symbolism: Four pentacles belong to a storehouse whose door is ajar. Keeping a reserve can preserve life and work; making it accessible is another decision. The red loop can secure an opening without deciding forever who may enter.
cards.upright: A useful reserve; conservation; a boundary that protects something worth keeping.
cards.reversed: Protection becoming enclosure; a reserve too difficult to reach; opening without provision for replenishment.
cards.question: What should be kept, and how can it remain available?

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.title: The Interrupted Circuit
cards.symbolism: Five discs remain in a frame with a missing section. Two people work on a short red repair cord below it. Their effort matters without making the interruption disappear; assistance starts from the actual break.
cards.upright: Need recognized; practical assistance; beginning a repair with someone else.
cards.reversed: An inaccessible offer; trying to work around a break that needs attention; help mistaken for a complete repair.
cards.question: Where is support interrupted, and what could reach that point?

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.title: The Turning Table
cards.symbolism: Six pentacles stand on a table that can turn between two people. A resource changes meaning with its use and availability. Giving need not create an equal debt, and receiving need not decide a person's standing.
cards.upright: Resources made available; generosity that can be received; an exchange with room for differing needs.
cards.reversed: Help on unusable terms; exact repayment demanded of a gift; difficulty asking or accepting.
cards.question: What would make this offer useful to the person receiving it?

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.title: The Unhurried Yield
cards.symbolism: Seven rooted discs occupy different stages of a nursery. The tender can adjust the warmth, but not command a return. Attention includes knowing when to wait, when to intervene, and when a method needs changing.
cards.upright: Patient cultivation; checking conditions; a return allowed time to develop.
cards.reversed: Waiting without observation; abandoning a living process too soon; continuing only because effort has already been spent.
cards.question: What change would tell you to keep tending, or to try another way?

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.title: The Repeated Difference
cards.symbolism: Eight discs share a form and differ in their rims. A craftsperson measures one marked edge against what the hand has learned. Repetition can deepen attention when the differences are still being noticed.
cards.upright: Practice that changes the hand; careful finish; a standard refined through use.
cards.reversed: Repetition without learning; polish that delays completion; a standard detached from its purpose.
cards.question: What difference can you now notice that you once would have missed?

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.title: The Room To Flourish
cards.symbolism: Nine pentacles grow through a trellis beside a person at rest. The red tie is small enough to leave room for enjoyment. Sufficiency may permit a chosen pace without proving that the garden maintains itself.
cards.upright: Room to enjoy what has been cultivated; practical independence; a pace you can choose.
cards.reversed: Guarding the appearance of sufficiency; isolation mistaken for freedom; maintenance crowding out enjoyment.
cards.question: What does having enough allow you to do, or stop doing?

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.title: The Common Inheritance
cards.symbolism: Ten pentacles support an open threshold while a key passes between generations. What is handed on includes access and the ability to maintain it. Continuity need not preserve every previous arrangement.
cards.upright: A resource made durable; stewardship handed on; access extended beyond its present keeper.
cards.reversed: Inheritance without usable access; preservation that prevents necessary change; a future burden left unnamed.
cards.question: What should be handed on, and what freedom should accompany it?

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.title: The First Sample
cards.symbolism: The apprentice turns one pentacle to see its edge. Wood grain and mineral veins make the object more than its face, and the red mark locates something to inspect. Learning begins with this particular sample.
cards.upright: Tactile curiosity; a practical question; learning from material evidence.
cards.reversed: A label replacing examination; collecting specimens without attending to them; conclusions wider than the sample.
cards.question: What can this particular object teach you?

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.title: The Kept Appointment
cards.symbolism: The courier carries a single pentacle in a cradle whose repair remains visible. Folded wings leave the pace deliberate. Reliability includes protecting what is carried and noticing when the means of carrying it need care.
cards.upright: A commitment kept through practical attention; measured progress; delivery with care.
cards.reversed: Routine continuing after conditions change; loyalty to a schedule that damages its purpose; neglect of the carrying structure.
cards.question: What needs tending so that you can arrive with this intact?

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.title: The Kept Warmth
cards.symbolism: The queen adjusts a source of warmth and tests what it provides. One pentacle belongs to the vessel, making care a material arrangement rather than an unlimited personal quality. Provision can include the person providing it.
cards.upright: Practical care; provision adjusted to need; comfort that can be sustained.
cards.reversed: Care expected without replenishment; comfort that cannot be adjusted; overlooking the keeper's needs.
cards.question: What would make this care sustainable for everyone involved?

cards.name: King of Pentacles
cards.title: The Repairable Estate
cards.symbolism: The king works on the mechanism that carries the pentacle. A red pin can be withdrawn so the assembly remains repairable. Responsibility includes preserving the ability to change what currently works.
cards.upright: Material competence; stewardship that maintains access and repair; resources used with foresight.
cards.reversed: Possession substituted for competence; a working arrangement sealed against repair; maintenance indefinitely deferred.
cards.question: What must remain open to repair if this is to endure?
